rows.title_full: AN ACT EFFECTIVELY AUTHORIZING THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT TO BAN AND AVERT THE  PRACTICE OF PRIVATE COMPANIES OF CONTRACTUALIZATION OF EMPLOYMENT AND ANY FORM OF FLEXIBILIZATION OF LABOR THEREBY ASSISTING SAID COMPANIES TOWARD A SHIFT TO REGULARIZATION OF EMPLOYMENT AND SECURITY OF TENURE FOR CONTRACTUAL WORKERS, LABORERS, AND EMPLOYEES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the practice in any public agency or private company the idea of circumventing the law in order to withhold benefits, privileges, and other emoluments accruing to bona fide and eligible
employees through the scheme of contractualization which is in principle a form of underemployment.

Intends to ban contractualization (any predetermined period of labor time or work); the discretion
to remove non-regulars without valid ground; and any form of flexible labor arrangement inimical to 
the workers and employees in private companies and veer toward the regularization of employees.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07036

rows.author: J122
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 141, 142 AND 143 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997
rows.abstract:
Aims to: raise additional revenues to fund the Universal Health Care (UHC) Program; reduce consumption of alcohol products; and to address the perceived inequity on the excise tax collections on alcohol and tobacco products.

Proposes to:  a) increase the indexation of excise tax rates on alcohol products from 4% to 7% annually; b) removes the distinction between fermented liquors brewed in microbreweries and in factories for simpler tax administration; c) exempts cooking wines containing a salt content of not less than 1.5 G/100 ML from excise tax; and d) imposes a biannual price survey to determine the net retail price of distilled spirits and sparkling wines.
rows.status: Republic Act RA11467 enacted on 2020-01-22

rows.abstract:
Aims to address the need to streamline the government's interface with business to encourage investment and one of the needed reforms is the optimization of the grant of incentives to industries critical to economic development.

Proposes to minimize redundant incentives if not to totally removed, to give way for more productive ones and seeks to entice increased investments even as it minimizes the revenue foregone from the grant of incentives. 

Intends to pursue a market-responsive investment regime and grant investment incentives that encourage long-term and recurrent investment promoting substantial social and economic spillovers and equitable development across income classes and across provinces.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING BUDGET REFORM THAT WILL ENSURE THE EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF FUNDS FOR BOTH THE NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROMOTING VILLAGE EMPOWERMENT, ENABLING THEM TO BE AN EFFECTIVE INSTRUMENT IN ATTAINING INCLUSIVE GROWTH, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to address existing gaps, among which is the measly sum of LGU share in the National Budget
where LGU shares, through the allocation to LGUs and IRA translates only to a mere 15% of the 
National Budget.

Proposes to institutionalize rational and equitable budget distribution for LGU development
for them to be active participants in national building.

States that the amount allocated to the LGUs will be referred to as the \"Local Development Fund
(LDF), which will be divided among the different political subdivisions solely for developmental 
projects, activities and programs (PAPs) based on the approved Comprehensive Development Plans
(CDPs).
